statement: A solid is built by stacking 1 cm cubes on a 4 by 4 grid on a table. The stack heights, back row first, each row left to right, are 3, 2, 2, 1; 2, 2, 1, 1; 2, 1, 1, 0; 1, 1, 0, 0. What is its surface area in square centimetres, including the faces on the table?

choices.misconception: I added the areas of the top, front and side views but forgot the matching bottom, back and other side.
I used the whole 4 by 4 square, 16, for the views from above and below, though three squares of the grid are empty.
I counted 6 faces for each of the 20 cubes and forgot that faces glued to another cube are hidden.
I left out the 13 faces resting on the table.

hints: Look at the solid from each of the six directions.
The stacks never get taller as you move forward or to the right, so the solid has no hollows: each square seen from any of the six directions is exactly one face. Add up the six views.
From above and from below you see 13 squares. From the front and from the back you see 3 + 2 + 2 + 1. From either side you see 3 + 2 + 2 + 1.

solutions.reliable: Count the faces direction by direction. Top: each of the 13 non-empty stacks shows one top face, and the bottom also has 13 faces on the table. Front: in each column the stacks get no taller towards the front, so every step down shows its own faces and the column shows as many front faces as its tallest stack: 3 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 8, and the back also shows 8. Each side, in the same way, shows 3 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 8. Total 13 + 13 + 8 + 8 + 8 + 8 = 58 square centimetres. The transferable idea: for a solid with no hollows, the surface area is twice the sum of the top, front and side views.
solutions.elegant: Check by gluing: the 20 cubes have 120 faces. There are 7 places where one cube sits on another and 24 places where two cubes touch side by side, 31 joins in all, and each join hides 2 faces. So 120 - 62 = 58.

whyOnTest: Tests reading a solid from its views: with no hollows, each view shows each outer face once, so the six views give the whole surface.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
